SEARCH
Package org.aeonbits.owner

Annotation Type Config.Prefix

Enclosing interface:
Config
@Retention(RUNTIME) @Target(TYPE) @Documented public static @interface Config.Prefix
Specifies a prefix that is prepended to the keys of all the properties declared in the annotated interface.

The prefix applies to the key derived from the method name as well as to the one specified with Config.Key: given @Prefix("server."), the method String name(); is looked up as server.name, and @Key("host.name") String host(); is looked up as server.host.name.

The prefix is not inherited by sub-interfaces: every method takes the prefix of the interface where it is declared, so the prefix of a sub-interface does not leak onto the methods it inherits, and the methods declared in a super-interface keep the prefix of that super-interface at any depth of the hierarchy. This is the rule every annotation describing the methods of an interface follows - Config.Mandatory, Config.Sensitive, Config.Separator, Config.TokenizerClass and Config.PreprocessorClasses with it - and this one is where it was first written down. See the documentation, Where an annotation counts.

The prefix is subject to variable expansion just like the rest of the key, so @Prefix("servers.${env}.") is a valid prefix.

The prefix is concatenated to the key literally, and no separator is added in between: ending it with the separator you want to use, typically a dot, is the recommended way to write it, but a prefix that does not end with one is a valid naming scheme rather than an error, and is left alone.

The prefix can be switched off for a single method or for a whole interface with @DisableFeature(DisableableFeature.PREFIX).

A prefix can also be configured on the Factory through the owner.key.prefix and owner.key.prefix.from.package properties, for the interfaces that do not declare one of their own. This annotation, being the explicit statement of the two, wins over it rather than being appended to it, while @DisableFeature(PREFIX) switches off both.

On a nested configuration interface the two compose instead, the path the object hangs from coming first: the path says where the object was hung and this annotation says how that object names its own keys, so neither is a default the other overrides. An interface carrying a prefix therefore carries it along when nested, and @DisableFeature(PREFIX) switches off the path too.

Since:
2.0.0
